scenario: LSCP.2.4.1 / LSCP.3.1 steps 6-7 -- an activation with an `after` tail keeps its `scope activation` fact until the timer fires, then retracts it. `gated` emits a Lock and arms `after 1_s`; the Lock lives across the async tail, so `watch` fires on the first pump and emits a ttl Seen (which a Lock retracted at the synchronous end of the RHS could not produce). At 2_s the follow-up fires, emits Done, and discharges its timer, which is the completion path: the Lock goes with it (LSCP.3.3, idempotent). Pin: fact_count 3 -- Trig + Seen + Done. 2 would be the Lock retracted too early (no Seen); 4 would be the Lock never retracted.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

schema Lock scope activation:
    entity_id: String

schema Seen scope ttl 1_h:
    entity_id: String

schema Done scope ttl 1_h:
    entity_id: String

rule gated:
    Trig
->
    emit Lock entity_id: "x"
    after 1_s:
        emit Done entity_id: "x"

rule watch:
    Lock l
->
    emit Seen entity_id: l.entity_id
